title: Dimension of an irreducible locally algebraic scheme over a field
statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $X$ be an irreducible scheme [def-weil-irreducible-components] whose structure morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Then $\dim U=\dim X$ for every nonempty open subset $U\subseteq X$, and $\dim_x(X)=\dim X$ for every $x\in X$, where $\dim$ is the topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] and $\dim_x$ is the dimension at a point [def-kun-dimension].

proof.text: (Reduction to $X$ integral.) Let $i:X_{\mathrm{red}}\to X$ be the reduction of $X$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction]. By [lem-weil-pbc-reduction-universal-homeomorphism] (with $X'=X$), $X_{\mathrm{red}}$ is reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme] and $i$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] which is a homeomorphism of underlying spaces (indeed the identity on underlying sets). Hence $X_{\mathrm{red}}$ is irreducible [def-weil-irreducible-components] (being homeomorphic to $X$), so nonempty, reduced and irreducible, i.e. integral [def-pc-integral-scheme]. A closed immersion is an immersion, hence locally of finite type [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-base-change-lft] (2), so the composite $X_{\mathrm{red}}\xrightarrow{i}X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] (e). Every assertion of the lemma concerns only the topological space of $X$ (the Krull dimensions of open subsets with the subspace topology [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], [def-kun-subspace-topology], and $\dim_x$ [def-kun-dimension], defined from them), and $i$ is a homeomorphism carrying nonempty opens to nonempty opens and preserving these dimensions [lem-weil-pbc-homeomorphism-krull-dimension]. Hence it suffices to prove the lemma for $X_{\mathrm{red}}$; from now on $X$ is integral and locally of finite type over $k$. (This is the source's parenthetical 'strictly speaking you have to replace $X$ by its reduction'.)

source.place: Varieties, Lemma 0A21 (lemma-dimension-locally-algebraic), proof of part (3), last sentence: 'strictly speaking you have to replace X by its reduction before applying the lemma'

proof.text: (All nonempty affine opens have one dimension $d$.) Since $X$ is integral it is nonempty; pick $x_0\in X$ and, by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis], an affine open $W_0\ni x_0$; put $d=\dim W_0$. By [lem-sc-integral-locally-algebraic-affine-opens-dimension], every nonempty open $W\subseteq X$ whose open subscheme is affine [def-weil-affine-spectrum] has $\dim W=\dim W_0=d$. (The source proves this by choosing a closed point $x\in W\cap W_0$, which exists since $X$ is Jacobson (Varieties 0478), and applying Algebra 00OS: $\dim W=\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}=\dim W_0$; that argument is the content of the cited node, which is closed by the slopmaster2 declaration AlgebraicGeometry.IsAffineOpen.topologicalKrullDim_eq_of_isIntegral.)

source.place: Varieties, Lemma 0A21 (lemma-dimension-locally-algebraic), proof of part (3), first sentences: 'It suffices to show that any two nonempty affine opens U, U' of X have the same dimension ... Pick a closed point x of X with x in U cap U' ... Then dim(U) = dim(O_{X,x}) = dim(U')'

proof.text: ($\dim U\geq d$.) Let $U\subseteq X$ be a nonempty open subset and $x\in U$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis] there is an affine open $W$ with $x\in W\subseteq U$; it is nonempty, so $\dim W=d$ by step 2. As $W\subseteq U\subseteq X$ are open, $\dim W\leq\dim U$ [lem-weil-pbc-open-subspace-dimension-monotone]. Hence $d\leq\dim U$.

source.place: Varieties, Lemma 0A21 (lemma-dimension-locally-algebraic), proof of part (3), the reduction to affine opens

proof.text: ($\dim U\leq d$; the source's parenthetical 'any finite chain of irreducible subsets meets an affine open'.) Let $U\subseteq X$ be a nonempty open subset, with the subspace topology [def-kun-subspace-topology]. By [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-supremum-local-dimensions] applied to the space $U$, $\dim U=\sup_{x\in U}\dim_x(U)$, where $\dim_x(U)$ is the minimum of $\dim U'$ over the open neighbourhoods $U'$ of $x$ in $U$ [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point]. For $x\in U$ choose by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis] an affine open $W$ of $X$ with $x\in W\subseteq U$; then $W$ is an open neighbourhood of $x$ in $U$, and its subspace topology from $U$ is its subspace topology from $X$, so $\dim_x(U)\leq\dim W=d$ by step 2. Hence $\dim U\leq d$.

source.place: Varieties, Lemma 0A21 (lemma-dimension-locally-algebraic), proof of part (3), parenthetical '(any finite chain of irreducible subsets meets an affine open)'; the argument is that of Topology, Lemma 0B7I (lemma-dimension-supremum-local-dimensions)

proof.text: (First assertion.) By steps 3 and 4, $\dim U=d$ for every nonempty open $U\subseteq X$; taking $U=X$ (nonempty) gives $\dim X=d$. Hence $\dim U=\dim X$ for every nonempty open $U\subseteq X$.

(Second assertion.) Let $x\in X$. By definition [def-kun-dimension], $\dim_x(X)=\min\{\dim U: x\in U\subseteq X\text{ open}\}$. Every such $U$ contains $x$, so is nonempty, and has $\dim U=\dim X$ by step 5. The set of values is therefore $\{\dim X\}$ and $\dim_x(X)=\dim X$.
